3. In this Case the Respondent No. 2 Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation ("HBFC") filed an application under Article 27 of the Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation Order, 1973 (President's Order No.7 of 1973) (hereinafter to be referred as "PO 7 of 1973"). In filing the said application before the District Judge, Khulna for realization of loan against the petitioner as opposite party, HBFC stated, inter-alia, that the petitioner applied for loan amounting to Taka 8,00,000 and, accordingly, on receiving a loan of Taka 7,87,000 constructed a house on the land mortgaged with the HBFC. That application being heard ex parte was allowed by Judgment and Order of 3-5-1997 and consequentially based on the same a decree for sale was signed on 10-5-1997. HBFC having, thereafter, filed an application for execution vide Execution Case No. 75 of 1998 in that very court, that phase of the execution proceedings however, ended in terms of a "solenama" executed on 5-4-1999 before the Joint District Judge Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna. An Order of disposal was recorded by the said Artha Rin Adalat on 7-4-1999. The petitioner contend that after the disposal of the said execution case HBFC filed another Execution Case No. 121 of2002 on 21-10-2002 under Order XXI, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure ("Code") in the Court of the. District Judge, Khulna for execution of decree by selling mortgaged property. This Court notes from the record that the District Judge sent the execution case for disposal to the Artha Rin Adalat. 

 5. It is at that juncture that the petitioner contending the execution proceedings to constitute malice in law and in an effort to deter the mortgaged land from being sold in auction sought relief before this Court by moving this Application. HBFC in responding to the Rule on questions of fact asserts that it was only upon the petitioner being in breach of the "solenama" of 5- 4-1999 that the HBFC took initiatives to file Execution Case No. 121 of 2002 under Order XXI, rule 11 of the Code for executing the ex parte decree of the District Judge of 3-5-1997. 

 7. In these facts and circumstances, this Court notes a factual gar that has not been addressed by the petitioner or the HBFC in the Application or Affidavit-in-Opposition. This pertains to the exact time and manner in which Execution Case No. 75 of 1998 came to be transferred to the Court of the Joint District Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna before whom the "solenama" was executed on 5-4-1999 as otherwise admitted by both parties. Indeed it is evident from the record that upon the contended breach of such "solenama" by the petitioner, HBFC did file Execution Case No. 121 of 2002 by appealing to the provisions of the Code before the Court of District Judge, but this time around the Court of the District Judge itself by an order found inscribed on HBFC's application initiated a transfer of the Execution Case to the Artha Rin Adalat in the following terms:
